chunks: He said: Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn Umar al-Ji'abi narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Mudarik ibn Tamam al-Shaybani narrated to us, saying: Zakariya ibn al-Hakam Abu Yahya al-Rasbi narrated to us, saying: Khalaf ibn Tamim narrated to us, saying: Bakr ibn Habish narrated from Abu Shaybah, from Abdul Malik ibn Umar, from Abu Qurrah, from Salman al-Farisi (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said to me:

"O Salman, when you wake up in the morning, say: 'O Allah, You are my Lord, there is no partner for You. We have entered the morning, and the kingdom belongs to Allah, there is no partner for Him.' Say it three times. And when you enter the evening, say the same, for they will atone for the sins committed between them."

key_terms.اللَّهُمَّ: An intensive vocative form addressing Allah, used exclusively in supplication (du'a). It combines 'Allah' with 'humma' and carries a tone of earnest invocation.
key_terms.الْمُلْك: Refers to absolute dominion and authority over all creation. Attributing al-Mulk to Allah alone affirms His complete sovereignty.
key_terms.خَطِيئَة: A moral wrongdoing or error. In this context, it refers to minor sins that can be expiated through regular acts of worship and remembrance.
key_terms.شَرِيك: One who shares in divinity or lordship. Negating any 'sharik' for Allah is a fundamental declaration of tawhid (monotheism) in Islam.
key_terms.يُكَفِّرْنَ: From the root k-f-r in form II, meaning to cover or wipe away sins. Here it indicates that the supplication erases sins committed between the morning and evening recitations.

ai.seo_question: What supplication did the Prophet teach Salman al-Farisi to say every morning and evening?
ai.summary: The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) instructs Salman al-Farisi to recite a specific supplication upon waking in the morning and upon entering the evening. The du'a affirms Allah's sole lordship and sovereignty with no partner, and the Prophet promises that repeating it three times in the morning and evening will atone for the sins committed in between. This teaching reflects the prophetic emphasis on beginning and ending each day with remembrance of Allah's oneness (tawhid) and seeking His forgiveness.
